title: robotindex Models & Data Entry
description: One entry in data/models-data.json — the AI/software substrate underneath physical robots, as opposed to the robots themselves (Directory) or the mods/firmware for a specific product (Builds & Mods). Draft schema, not yet as battle-tested as builds-mods-entry.schema.json: expect fields to evolve as the page's first real content goes live. Unlike Builds & Mods, entries here are not required to have a public repository — a 'closed' world model has no source to link to, only a vendor's own product page, and that distinction is exactly what the schema needs to preserve rather than paper over.

id.description: Stable unique id, never renamed once published.

tab.description: Which top-level tab this renders under. 'models' was added once Manipulation Models and Affective & Social Interaction outgrew the datasets tab — a tab labelled Datasets holding things that are not datasets is the kind of misclassification this index exists to avoid.

category.description: Sub-grouping within a tab. world-models entries must be 'Open' or 'Closed' — this is the load-bearing distinction on this page, since a 'Closed' entry is described from a vendor's own materials, not verified against source the way everything in Builds & Mods is. 'Manipulation Models' and 'Affective & Social Interaction' belong to the 'models' tab; the emotion corpora (EmpatheticDialogues, ESConv, MELD) stay under 'datasets' because they are datasets.

access.description: Whether this entry can be checked against real public source material (Open) or is described only from a vendor's own claims (Closed). For world-models entries this always matches `category` and is shown via the page's Open/Closed columns. For simulation-training, models and datasets entries — where every entry so far has a real, disclosed license even when gated or restrictive — it's shown as a small prefix on the license badge instead, so the same trust distinction stays visible without a second set of columns. Note this field answers 'can it be checked', not 'can it be used commercially': ManiSkill is Open here while its asset library is CC BY-NC.

license.description: Plain-language license/access status. Not gated to OSI licenses the way Builds & Mods' opensource tab is — but must be accurate: 'Proprietary', 'Gated — approval required', 'CC BY-NC 4.0', 'MIT', a specific custom license name, etc. Never left vague when the real answer is a restriction. Split terms are stated in full — 'Apache-2.0 (code) / CC BY-NC 4.0 (asset library)' — because the GitHub API only reports the root LICENSE file and will under-report a restriction that applies to the part most people actually want.

link.description: Canonical source. A GitHub/Codeberg repo when one exists (Open world models, Simulation & Training, most Datasets); a vendor's own product/docs page when it doesn't (Closed world models, gated datasets like Ego4D).

sourcing.description: Where the license and description came from, and what could not be confirmed. Optional for now so existing entries stay valid, but intended to become required once backfilled — every product record already carries one, and the absence of it here is the main reason this half of the index reads as a list rather than a verified index. Say what actually happened: 'Licence read from the repo's LICENSE file via the GitHub API (2026-09-28)' is honest; 'verified' is not, unless someone read it.

verifiedOn.description: ISO date the sourcing note was last checked. Separate from the prose so staleness can be queried rather than read. Licenses get changed and repos get archived; an undated license claim is worthless within a year.
